---
title: "Domains"
subtitle: "The model domains and their grids"
---

All datasets are made on the same model domains and grids, defined in
[`shared/domains.toml`](https://github.com/fesmc/FesmData/blob/main/shared/domains.toml).

## Concepts

A **domain** is a region on a map projection (polar stereographic, transverse Mercator
such as UTM, or Albers equal-area) with a **base grid**, its finest resolution, e.g.
ANT-500M for Antarctica. The **coarser grids** of the domain are made from the base grid
by merging whole cells, e.g. ANT-1KM to ANT-32KM. All grids of a domain are therefore
nested: every coarse cell is made of whole base cells, and the datasets on them are
exact conservative means of the base grid.

A **crop** is a smaller region inside a domain, cut from its grids, at the same
resolutions or some of them, e.g. Greenland, a crop of GreenlandPaleo. Its extent is
that of its grid at the base resolution; at each coarser resolution its grid is the
cells of the domain grid that overlap this extent, so adding a resolution does not
change the others.

A **nest** is a smaller domain inside a domain, on the same projection, with a finer
base grid of its own, made from the sources like any domain, e.g. Jakobshavn (250 m) in
GreenlandPaleo (500 m). At the resolutions it shares with its parent, its grids are the
cells of the parent grids that overlap its extent, so that its 500 m grid is a part of
GRL-PAL-500M.

A domain is **active** if its products are made and released. An inactive domain is
defined, but left out of the releases (see [Inactive domains](#inactive-domains)).

Each domain, crop and nest has an output **folder** under `$FESMDATA_PRODUCTS`, which is
also its name in `fesmdata.jl` and on the website (e.g. Antarctica, Thwaites), and a
**key**, the prefix of the names of its grids (e.g. ANT, THW).

## Domains, crops and nests

The **overview figures** show, for each Topo product of a domain (default products,
then variants; of its parent, for a crop), its bed, surface and ice thickness together
with the regions, zones and basins of the domain, on one of its finer grids. They are
large and open on their own.

## Ice-sheet domains and nests

Antarctica (ANT, 500 m to 32 km), GreenlandPaleo (GRL-PAL, 500 m to 32 km; Greenland and the
surrounding ocean and land, for glacial cycles) and North (NH, 2-32 km; the Northern
Hemisphere ice sheets) are on polar stereographic projections. Greenland (GRL) is a crop
of GreenlandPaleo, and Laurentide (LIS) and Eurasia (EIS) are crops of North.

The crops of Antarctica and the nests of Greenland cover single drainage basins, with
their ice shelves or fjords and 50 km around them: in Antarctica the Amundsen Sea
Embayment (ASE, at 500 m to 32 km), the Thwaites (THW) and Pine Island (PIG)
glaciers, the Filchner-Ronne (FRIS), Ross (ROSS) and Amery (AMY) ice shelves with the
grounded ice within 300 km upstream of them, and the Wilkes Subglacial Basin (WSB),
at 500 m and 1 km; in Greenland Jakobshavn Isbrae (JAK), the
Northeast Greenland Ice Stream (NEGIS), and the Petermann (PET) and Helheim (HEL)
glaciers, at 250 m, 500 m and 1 km.

## Mountain-glacier domains

The mountain-glacier domains cover the extent of their glaciers at the Last Glacial
Maximum, each on the projection used for glacier modelling in its region, with base
grids of 250 m (500 m for Svalbard) and a 2 km grid:

- **Pyrenees** (PYR, UTM 31N).
- **Patagonia** (PAT, UTM 18S), from 38°S to Cape Horn, with crops of the Northern and
  Southern Patagonian Icefields (NPI, SPI, 250 m), and nests of single icefields at 50,
  100 and 250 m: the San Rafael Glacier (SRG, whose 250 m grid is the v1 SRG-250M grid),
  Gran Campo Nevado (GCN) and the Cordillera Darwin Icefield (CDI).
- **Himalaya** (HIM, Albers equal-area of High Mountain Asia), the Himalaya, Karakoram
  and Hindu Kush, with a nest of the Drang Drung Glacier (DDG, Zanskar) at 25, 50, 100
  and 250 m.
- **Alps** (ALP, UTM 32N).
- **Svalbard** (SVB, UTM 33N).
- **New Zealand** (NZ, NZTM2000).

## Global grids

The Global domain (GLOBAL) has global lon-lat grids at 0.1°, 0.25°, 0.5°, 1°, 2° and 5°
(GLOBAL-0.1DEG, ..., GLOBAL-5DEG), each with cell edges at -180° and -90°. They are not
nested (0.25° is not a multiple of 0.1°). It also has Gaussian grids, named by their
spectral truncation, e.g. GLOBAL-T170 (512 x 256, as used by VILMA), made only for the
products that need them. Global sources are remapped onto these grids, so that all
global products share them.

## Grid names and grid files

Grids are named after the key of their domain (or crop, or nest) and their resolution:
`ANT-8KM`, `GRL-PAL-500M`, `DDG-25M`, `GLOBAL-0.5DEG`. A grid name thus also gives its
domain. Every grid has its own folder, with its grid files and all datasets on that
grid:

```
$FESMDATA_PRODUCTS/<folder>/<GRID>/
    grid_<GRID>.txt         grid description (cdo)
    <GRID>_grid.nc          x, y, lon, lat and area of the cells
    <GRID>_TOPO-<product>.nc, <GRID>_REGIONS.nc, <GRID>_GHF-<source>.nc, ...
```

The grid files come with every dataset on the grid.

## Which datasets are on which grids

Topo and Regions are made on every grid of every active domain, crop and nest, from
the high-resolution sources. Regions also has the masks of the nests and crops of a
domain on all grids of the domain, its crops and nests (`<GRID>_DOMAINS.nc`, see
[Regions](datasets/regions.qmd#domains)).

The thematic datasets (GHF, Velocity, SMB, ...) are made by remapping published maps,
which are much coarser than the base grids. They are made only on the grids that add
information: as a rule, no grid is finer than about a quarter of the spacing of the
source, e.g. 16 km and 0.5° for sources at 1-2°, 8 km and 0.25° for sources at
0.25-0.5°, 4 km for most others, and the 2 km grids of the mountain-glacier domains. A
model that needs a finer grid can remap online.

They are released on the domains, and on the crops that a product lists (e.g.
Greenland, Laurentide and Eurasia, or a Greenland-only source on Greenland). The other
crops and the nests lie on the grids of their domain, so they get the thematic datasets
by cropping those of their domain (or of a crop that contains them, e.g. Greenland for
Jakobshavn), on demand, when they are downloaded (see
[Nests and crops](download.qmd#nests-and-crops)). [Products](products.qmd) shows which
dataset is on which domain.

## Inactive domains

A domain can be defined but not used yet (`active = false` in `shared/domains.toml`;
none at present): its grids and products are made only on request, and it is left out
of the releases and figures. To have one made and released, open an
[issue](https://github.com/fesmc/FesmData/issues).
